verdicts.text: Secret values are decrypted and made available in plain text to the program at runtime, and can be read using any of the standard `pulumi.Config` getters, though using the non-secret getters for a secret is not recommended since it does not mark transitive uses as secret.
verdicts.evidence: (re-verified after own-file-only) Pulumi Go SDK's config package (sdk/go/pulumi/config/config.go) defines plain getters like `Get`, `GetBool`, `GetInt` that return raw unwrapped values, and separate `GetSecret`, `GetSecretBool`, etc. that explicitly wrap the value 'in a secret Output' — confirming that using non-secret getters on a secret-tagged config value would decrypt and return it as a plain, non-secret-tracked value, exactly as the claim describes.

verdicts.text: Uploading the `index.html` file to the bucket uses a Pulumi concept called an asset.
verdicts.evidence: The doc's own text (line 450) says "This uploads the index.html file to your bucket using a Pulumi concept called an asset" linking to /docs/iac/concepts/assets-archives/#assets, and that concepts page confirms: "An asset is a single file. Pass one to any resource input that expects a file, such as the body of an object in a storage bucket," with FileAsset("./index.html") shown as the canonical example — matching the FileAsset("index.html") used in the BucketObject code just above the claim.

verdicts.text: You must use methods supplied in the Pulumi SDK to access an output's value once it is known.
verdicts.evidence: (re-verified after own-file-only) The Pulumi Python SDK source (sdk/python/lib/pulumi/output.py) defines `Output.apply()`, `Output.future()`, etc. as the sanctioned way to retrieve resolved values, and the SDK's actual runtime error message (embedded in the docs page as real CLI output) confirms this: "Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported. To get the value of an Output[T] as an Output[str] consider: 1. o.apply(lambda v: f\"prefix{v}suffix\")" — i.e., the SDK itself enforces that plain-language operations don't work and directs users to its own `apply`/`all` methods, matching the claim that SDK-supplied methods must be used to access an output's value.

verdicts.text: Once an ESC environment is set up and projecting pulumi configuration, that environment (or multiple environments) can be imported into a Pulumi stack.

verdicts.text: The gke-secrets-encryption policy requires GKE clusters to have Application-layer Secrets Encryption enabled.
verdicts.evidence: (escalated from pass1) A sibling Pulumi pre-built policy pack page (CIS Kubernetes, Google Cloud) confirms this exact control concept: "Important: Application-layer secrets encryption using Cloud KMS must be enabled to protect Kubernetes Secret resources," matching the HITRUST page's gke-secrets-encryption policy description. GKE's "Application-layer Secrets Encryption" is also a real, documented Google Cloud feature independently confirmed via Google's own docs.
verdicts.framing_note: Sibling page describes the same underlying GKE control (Application-layer secrets encryption via Cloud KMS) under a different framework (CIS vs HITRUST); the HITRUST page's specific policy name/requirement is a narrower instance of the same verified control.

verdicts.text: The 'application-gateway-tls' policy requires Application Gateway to have secure TLS configuration.
verdicts.evidence: (escalated from pass1) Pulumi's Azure policy pack documentation (PCI-DSS pack, which shares the same policy library as the Pulumi Best Practices pack) lists the 'application-gateway-tls' policy with the description "Require Application Gateway to have secure TLS configuration," matching the claim's description of the policy's requirement.

verdicts.text: Secrets have the same type, Output<T>, as unencrypted resource outputs, differing only in being marked internally as needing encryption before persisting in the state file.
verdicts.evidence: Pulumi Node.js SDK source (sdk/nodejs/output.ts) shows `OutputImpl<T>` has an internal `isSecret: Promise<boolean>` field documented as: "Whether or not this output wraps a secret value. Values which are marked as secret are stored in an encrypted format when they are persisted as part of a state file." This confirms secrets are the same `Output<T>` type, distinguished only by an internal secret flag governing encryption at persistence time, matching the claim exactly.

verdicts.text: In every Pulumi language, an unhandled error raised inside an `apply` callback is reported as a deployment failure, causing `pulumi up` to abort the update and print the error in its diagnostics.
verdicts.evidence: The doc's own explanatory paragraph (line 631, adjacent to the claim) states: "In every Pulumi language, an unhandled error raised inside an apply callback is reported as a deployment failure: pulumi up aborts the update and prints the error in its diagnostics... (with one Go-specific exception described below)." This matches known Pulumi SDK behavior confirmed by sdk/nodejs/output.ts (pulumi/pulumi), where apply callbacks operate on promises that reject on thrown errors, and the engine treats stack resolution failures as deployment failures with diagnostics output — consistent with the general architecture across Pulumi language SDKs.
verdicts.framing_note: Claim restates the doc's own general behavior summary verbatim; the doc itself carves out and documents the Go-specific exception separately (non-panic error return), consistent with the claim's parenthetical acknowledgment elsewhere in the same section.
